```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4)
library(cytoJointR)
has_compass <- requireNamespace("COMPASS", quietly = TRUE)
has_stan <- requireNamespace("cmdstanr", quietly = TRUE) &&
  !is.null(tryCatch(cmdstanr::cmdstan_version(error_on_NA = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL))
```

cytoJointR does not replace COMPASS or polyICSFlow. For each of their
features it either has its own counterpart or hands the work to the real
package through an adapter. This page lists the mapping, then shows where
the numbers differ and why.

## Feature mapping

| Tool | Feature | cytoJointR counterpart | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| COMPASS | Functionality score (FS) | `cj_compass()` returns native `compass_FS`; own signed scores: `cj_scores()` (`RMS`, `CPS`, `CCS`, ...) | adapter and own model |
| COMPASS | Polyfunctionality score (PFS) | `cj_compass()` returns native `compass_PFS`; own: `poly_absolute`, `poly_marginal`, `breadth` | adapter and own model |
| COMPASS | `Response()` | `cj_compass()` returns `compass_response_degree1` and `compass_response_degree2`; own: `p_positive` per pattern from `cj_patterns()` | adapter and own model |
| COMPASS | Mean-gamma heatmap | `cj_plot_compass()` draws COMPASS's own; own: `cj_plot_response_heatmap()` | adapter and own plot |
| COMPASS | Posterior differences | `COMPASS::PosteriorDiff()` works on `cj_compass()$fits`; own: `cj_scores()` and `cj_visit_change()` give signed draws-based differences | adapter (not wrapped) and own model |
| COMPASS | Category filters | `cj_compass(category_filter=)` applies COMPASS's default and reports what it removed in `$filters` | adapter |
| COMPASS | `GatingSet` input | `cj_from_gatingset()`; **not verified**, see below | unverified |
| COMPASS | Shiny app | none | deferred |
| polyICSFlow | Marker positivity | `cj_from_events(thresholds=)` and `cj_plot_pattern_scatter()` | own |
| polyICSFlow | `MarkerComb` table | `cj_from_polyicsflow()` reads `extractCellCounts()` output | adapter (tested on a hand-built table only) |
| polyICSFlow | Background-subtracted percentages | `cj_describe()$patterns$net_percent` (signed) and `net_percent_display` (clipped) | own |
| polyICSFlow | Heatmap | `cj_plot_pattern_heatmap()` | own |
| polyICSFlow | Exactly-n and at-least-n bars | `cj_plot_degree_bars(type = "exactly" / "at_least")` | own |
| polyICSFlow | 2D scatters | `cj_plot_pattern_scatter()` | own |

Two limits on that table.

* Shiny is deferred. Nothing in the package serves an interactive app.
* `cj_from_gatingset()` is unverified. `flowWorkspace` segfaults on the
  development host, even after rebuilding its dependency chain from source,
  so the function has never run. Use `cj_from_counts()` or
  `cj_from_events()` if you can export counts or events yourself.

## Where the numbers differ

**Clipping.** polyICSFlow clips background-subtracted percentages at 0.
cytoJointR keeps the signed value in `net_percent`. The clipped value is a
separate column, `net_percent_display`, for plots only, and `display_only`
marks the rows where clipping changed the number. No score or probability
uses it.

**COMPASS scores are not sign probabilities.** COMPASS FS, PFS and
`Response()` come from its responder mixture model. They are bounded
quantities with COMPASS's definitions. They are not cytoJointR's
`p_positive`, `p_negative` and `p_negligible`, and the two should not be
compared as if they were. The adapter never relabels one as the other. See
`docs/adr/0001-compass-parity-via-adapter.md` in the package source.

## Clipping in practice

```{r data}
# The default simulated effect is so strong that every donor responds in every
# pattern, which COMPASS's heatmap cannot draw. Weaken the stimulation effect.
args <- list(n_donors = 10, markers = c("IFNG", "TNF", "IL2"), stimulations = "CMV",
             visits = "v1", N = 1500, seed = 3)
gamma <- do.call(cj_simulate_counts, args)$truth$gamma
gamma["stim_CMV", ] <- gamma["stim_CMV", ] - 1.7
x <- do.call(cj_simulate_counts, c(args, list(truth = list(gamma = gamma))))$data
p <- cj_describe(x)$patterns
neg <- p[p$display_only, c("contrast_id", "pattern", "net_percent", "net_percent_display")]
head(neg)
```

These rows are the all-negative pattern, which loses cells to the positive
patterns. The signed value is negative and the display column shows 0.
Averaging the display column would bias the mean upward; the signed column
does not.

## COMPASS through the adapter

`cj_compass()` runs one `COMPASS::SimpleCOMPASS()` per stimulation, visit and
parent population. The chunk runs only when COMPASS is installed
(`r if (has_compass) "it is" else "it is not"` here).

```{r compass, eval = has_compass, message = FALSE}
# COMPASS warns that it cannot infer the marker count after its category filter.
cc <- suppressWarnings(cj_compass(x, iterations = 300, replications = 2, seed = 1))
head(cc$scores)
cc$filters[, c("group", "n_patterns", "n_removed", "removed")]
```

The filter line shows what COMPASS's default category filter removed. The
native `COMPASSResult` objects are in `cc$fits`, so any COMPASS function
works on them.

```{r compass-plot, eval = has_compass, fig.height = 5}
cj_plot_compass(cc)
```

Side by side with the signed score of the same contrast, when CmdStan is
also available:

```{r compare, eval = has_compass && has_stan, message = FALSE}
fit <- cj_fit(x, centered = TRUE, chains = 4, iter_warmup = 500, iter_sampling = 500,
              seed = 1, adapt_delta = 0.95, show_messages = FALSE)
eps <- c(RMS = 0.005, poly_absolute = 0.005, poly_marginal = 0.005, CPS = 0.02,
         CCS = 0.005, breadth = 0.05, marker_magnitude = 0.005)
sc <- cj_scores(fit, eps)
rms <- sc[sc$score == "RMS", c("contrast_id", "estimate", "p_positive")]
m <- merge(cc$scores[c("contrast_id", "compass_FS", "compass_PFS")], rms)
head(m)
```

`compass_FS` and `estimate` (the RMS net score) move together across donors here, but they are different quantities on different
scales, and `compass_FS` has no sign.

```{r no-compass, eval = !has_compass, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
cat("*COMPASS is not installed, so the adapter chunks were not run.*")
```
